display.purpose: Page h1 and hero titles only. LEMON MILK.

title.purpose: h3/h4 and every card title. Montserrat 700 — deliberately not LEMON MILK.

label.purpose: Eyebrows and small caps labels. Montserrat 700, 11px, 0.15em tracking, uppercase — per the four-role type decision recorded in tokens.css.

accent.purpose: Pinyon Script. At most one phrase per page, 30px or larger.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Feature imagery only. The 20 resting card/media shadows that once contradicted the Flat-At-Rest Rule have been removed; what remains is genuinely floating UI (sticky header, dropdown, search panel, map search).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Honoured, not decorative. The hero video must not play a frame under this preference, and its pause control stays operable.

narrative.overview:
Few elements, each one finished. A pearl earns attention by being small, complete and slightly luminous — not by being loud — and this system works the same way. Gold is the luster: rationed hard so that when it appears, on a rule, a numeral, an eyebrow, or one button, it still reads as precious. Royal blue carries the institutional weight. Everything else gets out of the way so photography of real sorors and real numbers can do the persuading.

The mood is warm and welcoming before it is impressive. A woman considering membership should feel invited, not audited; a foundation officer should find the evidence without hunting for it. Those two readings are not in tension here, because the warmth comes from generous space, unhurried line height (1.7 body), and real faces — not from soft language. Trust is earned with founding history, named leadership, and verified figures. Where a number does not exist, the layout accommodates its absence; it does not invent one.

Depth is tonal, not cast. The page advances through bands — white, cool slate, cream, then a royal gradient — and that stack is what creates hierarchy. Shadows are close to eliminated by intent.
keyCharacteristics: Gold as luster, never as surface — rationed to rules, numerals, labels and a single button
Royal and navy carry structure; the palette has no third accent
Depth from stacked tonal bands, not from shadow
Two display faces (LEMON MILK) over two text faces (Montserrat, Playfair), never more
Real photography and verified numbers over illustration and claims
AA contrast is a floor enforced by tests, not a review step

rules.name: The Rationed Luster Rule
rules.body: Gold covers well under 10% of any screen. If a composition needs more gold to feel finished, the composition is the problem.

rules.name: The Two-Golds Rule
rules.body: Gold that carries words is never --gold. It is --gold-text on light ground and --gold-bright on dark. --gold itself is for rules, fills, icons, and borders. Picking the wrong one is the single most common defect this system has produced.

rules.name: The No Third Accent Rule
rules.body: Royal and gold. Any additional hue must be argued for, not assumed.

rules.name: The Rhoer Reservation
rules.body: Yellow Gold #FFD700 belongs to the Rhoer Club only. Never use it in general design.

rules.name: The Shouting Rule
rules.body: LEMON MILK is all-caps by nature. h1, h2, eyebrows and big numerals — nothing else. Card titles and sub-heads are Montserrat 700. Promoting a card title to h2 for outline reasons would silently change its typeface; add a visually-hidden h2 instead.

rules.name: The One Signature Rule
rules.body: Pinyon Script appears at most once per page, at 30px or larger, on a high-emotion phrase. Never an eyebrow, a label, or body copy.

rules.name: The Four Faces Rule
rules.body: Four families is the ceiling, and it is already reached. Any fifth face is a regression.

rules.name: The No Fixed Track Rule
rules.body: Never size a grid track in bare pixels. Always minmax(min(Npx, 100%), 1fr).

rules.name: The 320 Rule
rules.body: 320px is a supported width, not an edge case. A long unbreakable headline in a narrow column is a layout bug, not a content problem.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat by default. If something needs to separate from its background, change the band tone or add a hairline before reaching for a shadow.

rules.name: The Pill-or-Nothing Rule
rules.body: Buttons are fully round. There are no 8px-radius buttons in this system.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Borders separate; they do not decorate. A border thicker than 1px on a rounded card reads as a template accent.

dos: Do use --gold-text (#8a6510) for gold type on white or cream, and --gold-bright (#f0cf5c) for gold type on royal or navy. Reserve plain --gold for rules, fills, icons and borders.
Do put navy text on any gold fill.
Do build separation from band tone and hairlines before reaching for a shadow.
Do write grid tracks as minmax(min(Npx, 100%), 1fr).
Do keep card titles and sub-heads in Montserrat 700, and add a visually-hidden h2 when an outline needs one.
Do use real SGRho photography — sisterhood, service, celebration.
Do cite real, verified numbers, and design around a number's absence rather than inventing it.
Do treat AA contrast as a build gate; the Playwright suite in tests/ enforces it across every route.
donts: Don't let this look like a generic nonprofit template — stock smiling-people photography, three icon boxes in a row, a donate bar, vague mission language. This is the confirmed anti-reference.
Don't let this look collegiate or athletic — varsity type, diagonal cuts, team-brand energy. Confirmed anti-reference.
Don't use gold as a background for body content.
Don't use Yellow Gold #FFD700; it is Rhoer Club only.
Don't introduce a fifth type family, or a third accent hue.
Don't set eyebrow or highlight color in a page-scoped selector.
Don't put a thick accent border on a rounded card.
Don't add a decorative font, clip art, sticker, or overlay, and never stretch, recolor, crop, or overlap the Shield.
Don't ship AI-generated imagery that misrepresents the marks, or publish ritual photography.
